q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT TMP.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(TMP.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM (SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, P.EMPLOYEE_ID, E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM EMPLOYEE E INNER JOIN PROJECT P ON E.EMPLOYEE_ID = P.EMPLOYEE_ID ) AS TMP GROUP BY TMP.PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT TMP.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(TMP.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM (SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, P.EMPLOYEE_ID, E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM EMPLOYEE E INNER JOIN PROJECT P ON E.EMPLOYEE_ID = P.EMPLOYEE_ID ) AS TMP GROUP BY TMP.PROJECT_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPLOYEE_ID, NAME, EXPERIENCE_YEARS) VALUES (1, 'Employee1', 5), (2, 'Employee2', 10), (3, 'Employee3', 15); INSERT INTO PROJECT (PROJECT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID) VALUES (101, 1), (101, 2), (102, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 groups by A.PROJECT_ID and then calculates the average of B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS, while Q2 first joins EMPLOYEE and PROJECT into a subquery TMP and then groups by TMP.PROJECT_ID to calculate the average of TMP.EXPERIENCE_YEARS. The difference arises from how the GROUP BY clause is applied in each query, which can lead to different results if there are multiple employees with the same project_id but different experience_years.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two employees with the same project_id but different experience_years. The difference in results will be observed when calculating the average experience years for that project_id.
